title: Flight Deck configuration
description: Configuration for the oc-flight-deck TUI plugin. Every key is optional: install the plugin and it works with no config file at all — a missing file is normal and silent. Copy flight-deck.example.jsonc to the one global path, ~/.config/opencode/flight-deck.jsonc ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/flight-deck.jsonc when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set), and edit; that single file applies to every project. There is no per-project lookup: a flight-deck.jsonc in a project root or in .opencode/ is not read. Comments and trailing commas are allowed. An invalid value is ignored, its default is restored, and a one-time toast names the key to fix — a typo can never break the TUI.

$schema.description: Points an editor or an AI at this file, which is the authoritative list of every option, type, default and valid value.

refresh.description: Milliseconds between ticks. Cost and tokens arrive with host events; anything derived from the clock — `elapsed`, the status spinner, and the caution thresholds — needs this timer. 100 turns the spinner once a second. 0 turns the ticker off entirely, which also freezes the annunciator (it works, but only updates on host events). Practical range 16–1000; 1–15 are treated as 16, while 0 is the deliberate off switch and is never clamped.

sidebar.description: The rail itself: the branding lines and the live rows.

enabled.description: Draw the sidebar rail at all. false leaves the plugin loaded but invisible.

lines.description: Fixed lines rendered above the live rows, in order. Branding or a separator. These render at full brightness; the live rows below them are dimmed. The fixed lines and the live rows together are capped at 24 — anything past that is dropped from the rail.

rows.description: Which live fields to draw, top to bottom. Any subset, any order — this is the single most useful thing to change. With `sidebar.persist` (the default) every named row always renders, using `sidebar.placeholder` until the host has data; with `persist: false` rows with no data are omitted entirely. Counted together with `sidebar.lines` against a 24-line cap on the whole rail.

persist.description: Render every field named in `sidebar.rows` as a persistent row, using `sidebar.placeholder` when the host has no data yet. True keeps the rail a stable shape that fills in as the session produces data; false restores the old behavior of omitting rows with no data.

placeholder.description: Value shown for a persistent row with no data yet. Used only when `sidebar.persist` is true. Must be a non-empty string; anything else falls back to the default em dash.

footer.description: A single line in the prompt footer. Off unless configured — writing any footer setting turns it on.

enabled.description: Show the footer line. Defaults to true if any other footer key is present, false if the footer section is absent.

text.description: The footer text. Max 120 characters; control characters are replaced with spaces.

caution.description: The annunciator: a warning row for the one failure nothing else can see. A hang emits no events at all, so this uses a clock and a baseline rather than a listener. Silent unless something has stopped moving. It reports observations, never verdicts — `shell running 8m41s`, not 'stuck' — and it never aborts, kills, retries or blocks anything.

enabled.description: Run the annunciator. false means the `caution` row never appears and no timer is spent on it.

toolWatchSeconds.description: A tool running longer than this draws a subdued ▲. 180s is longer than a slow build and short enough to notice before you start wondering. Lower it if you work on fast tools and want to catch stalls sooner.

toolCautionSeconds.description: A tool running longer than this becomes a real ⚠. Raised to match toolWatchSeconds if set below it, and reported.

turnWatchSeconds.description: A running session that has produced nothing for this long draws a ▲. Deliberately generous: a large reasoning model can think for minutes with nothing to show, which is indistinguishable from a wedge by the clock alone. Suppressed entirely while a tool or shell is running.

turnCautionSeconds.description: A quiet session becomes a real ⚠ after this long. Raised to match turnWatchSeconds if set below it, and reported.

repeatThreshold.description: How many identical consecutive calls count as a loop. Two is a retry; three is a pattern. Applies to both the repeat rule (identical successes) and the failure rule (identical errors).

exemptTools.description: Tools that are slow by nature, so slow is not an anomaly for them. Matched by exact name. Calibrated against 53,672 real tool calls: at the default threshold 307 calls exceed it and 218 of those are these tools — `subagent` alone crossed 152 times with a p99 of 14.7 minutes. Without this list the annunciator lights on every delegated task, which is how an alert gets ignored. Add your own long-running or orchestration tools here.

toast.description: Also raise a toast the first time a caution appears, once per distinct problem, re-arming when the session goes quiet. Off by default: the rail is the signal and a notification is an interruption. Worth enabling if you walk away from long runs.

layout.description: Row geometry. Change these when your terminal is unusually narrow or wide.

labelWidth.description: Width of the label column that every row pads to. 10 fits `caution` plus a space. Narrow it to fit more value on screen, widen it if you rename the labels.

barWidth.description: Cells in the `context` gauge — the filled/empty bar.

sparkWidth.description: Samples drawn in the `spark` row. The newest turns are kept, so narrowing it keeps the recent shape rather than the oldest. The row is this many cells wide, so a large value is a wide row — mind a narrow sidebar.

glyphs.description: The annunciator's characters. Change these when a terminal renders the defaults as a box, or at the wrong width — an ugly-but-readable panel beats an unreadable one. One or two characters each.

watch.description: Shown for a watch: something is slower than it should be, but below the caution threshold.

caution.description: Shown for a real caution. This is the row that has to read at a glance.

clear.description: Reserved for a future always-visible annunciator state. Not currently drawn: the row is absent when nothing is wrong.
